statement: Suppose f is locally Lipschitz on D, and, in its interior, 0 ≤ fj ≤ dj, 0 ≤ fv ≤ dv, fjk ≤ 0 (j ̸= k), fjv ≤ 0 in the distributional sense. The derivative bounds may instead be local bounds on each compact neighborhood under consideration; in that case all conclusions concerning boundedness are local. Then there are, up to null sets, uniquely determined locally bounded fields a1, . . . , an, D on R × I, with 0 ≤ aj ≤ dj and 0 ≤ D ≤ dv, having the following properties. 1. Strong traces. For almost every interior offset η ∈ K◦, the restrictions of the ambient gradients to Π(·) + η are defined almost everywhere. As η → 0 through such offsets, they converge strongly in L1 loc(di du) to (a1, . . . , an, D). For Q ⋐ Q′ ⋐ R × I this convergence has the bound ∥fα(Π(·) + η) − Aα∥L1(Q) ≤ CQ|η| + ωα,Q′ (CQ|η|), A = (a1, . . . , an, D), (6.9) where ωα,Q′ (r) → 0 is the L1 translation modulus of Aα on Q′. The constant depends only on the local derivative bounds, the clock speeds, and the two patches. 2. Measure identities. There exist locally finite nonnegative measures νjk = νkj, j ̸= k, and νjv on the plane such that Vjaj = −νjv − X k̸=j (ck − cj)νjk, ∂iD = − X j νjv. (6.10) For F = f ◦ Π, the weak derivatives are Fi = X j aj, Fu = X j cjaj + D. (6.11) 41 In particular, Vnan ≥ ∂iD (6.12) as measures. With qj = 1 + cn − cj, the full flux identity is − X j qjVjaj = X j<k (ck − cj)2 νjk + X j qjνjv. (6.13) 3. Affine approximation. There is a sequence hℓ ↓ 0 and a single null set N ⊂ R × I such that, for every (i, u) / ∈ N and every finite R, lim ℓ→∞ sup ξ∈K, |ξ|≤R f(Π(i, u) + hℓξ) − f(Π(i, u)) hℓ − X j aj(i, u)ξj − D(i, u)ξv = 0. (6.14) Only sufficiently large ℓ, for which the displayed label times belong to I, are used. The sequence may depend on f.
